prompt: A two-sided test of $H_0: p = 0.4$ versus $H_a: p \ne 0.4$ produces a test statistic of $z = 2.0$. Given that $P(Z > 2.0) = 0.0228$, what is the $p$-value? Round to four decimal places.
hint: A two-sided alternative counts BOTH tails: results as extreme as $2.0$ in either direction.

hints.text: A two-sided alternative counts BOTH tails: results as extreme as $2.0$ in either direction.
$p\text{-value} = P(Z > 2.0) + P(Z < -2.0)$, and the normal curve is symmetric.

explanation: The $p$-value is the probability, assuming $H_0$, of a statistic at least as extreme as the one observed.
For $H_a: p \ne 0.4$, "as extreme" means $|z| \ge 2.0$ — the upper tail AND the lower tail.
By symmetry each tail is $0.0228$, so the $p$-value is $0.0456$. At $\alpha = 0.05$ this would lead to rejecting $H_0$.

alternativeExplanations.title: One-sided vs two-sided
steps: If the alternative had been $p > 0.4$, the $p$-value would be just the upper tail: $0.0228$.
The $\ne$ alternative was chosen BEFORE seeing the data, so it must pay for both directions.
Doubling gives $0.0456$ — twice as hard to reach significance.
